text:
taylor: heads-up — proposal to split the single `route` telemetry field into `route_id` (stable canonical) + `route_label` (human-friendly). small doc at https://docs.internal/telemetry/route-split (WIP)
monica: curious — what's the primary motivation? index/cardinality issues? :thinking_face:
ravi: yes, dashboards and expensive GROUP BYs. route currently mixes user-provided labels and system ids, making cardinality explode. also breaks our quota routing when labels change.
jen: +1. we also see UI teams mapping label -> integration which is very brittle.
taylor: plan sketch: 1) accept dual-write for writes (both hosted and private ingesters), 2) add a read adapter that falls back to `route_label` for legacy rows, 3) run backfill job to populate route_id on historical rows, 4) add index and switch queries over in console.
sam: how do we do dual-write for older SDK versions? can't guarantee clients will send route_id immediately.
taylor: good point — ingestion will derive route_id when missing by calling a canonicalizer service with best-effort mapping. canonicalizer: map label -> id using latest alias table; results are stored as `route_id` on ingest; if unresolved, mark `route_id = ''` and backfill later.
monica: what about query compatibility? dashboards currently hit `WHERE route = 'foo'`.
ravi: we'll add a compatibility view `telemetry_routes_v2` with SQL like:

```
SELECT
  COALESCE(route_id, canonicalize_label(route_label)) AS route_key,
  other_fields...
FROM telemetry_events
```

so dashboards can switch to `route_key` without major rewrite.
jen: will that view be fast enough at scale? we have millions of events/day.
taylor: for perf we plan to backfill route_id and then create a covering index on (route_id, ts DESC) and a partial index for common labels. view is temporary for migration window.
sam: backfill strategy?
taylor: incremental shard job run as k8s CronJob with per-tenant parallelism and rate limiting. job marks rows as migrated in a migration table to be idempotent. rough SQL snippet for backfill worker:

```
UPDATE telemetry_events
SET route_id = canonicalize_label(route_label), migrated_v2 = true
WHERE route_id = ''
AND id BETWEEN $start AND $end
LIMIT 10000;
```

we'll use SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED to coordinate workers.
jen: risk: this will blow up write IOPS and interfere with streaming consumers.
ravi: suggestion: do backfill from cold storage export (parquet) into a bulk loader that writes directly to analytic table, then swap pointers.
monica: that seems safer but more involved. Do we have time for table swap gating?
taylor: timeline options: minimal (dual-write + view + slow backfill in 4 weeks) vs aggressive (export+bulk load + index swap in 2 weeks). need sign-off from infra.
sam: SLA/alerts — add alerts for migration lag and high replication lag. if backfill lag > 1h or DB CPU > 70% -> pause job.
jen: console UX: we should add a rollout flag in the console to let product teams opt-in to new route_key in dashboards. default to old behavior for 2 weeks post-migration.
ravi: quotas: routing is used to apply per-route quota profiles. We must ensure quota evaluation uses route_id once available; fallback to label otherwise. also need to keep history to recompute usage correctly for billing.
taylor: billing note: do not change aggregation windows mid-period. We'll compute quotas on `route_id` for new events, and for legacy events keep using label until backfilled, then run usage reconciliation in a delayed batch to reattribute tokens where necessary.
monica: does anyone object to adding a migration header `X-Route-Migration: 1` at ingest so we can detect traffic from updated clients?
sam: sgtm. will add to SDK changelog.
jen: security/privacy check — does route_label contain PII? if so, cannot be kept in plain column. any examples?
monica: a handful of customers used emails as labels during early beta. we must scrub or hash them when copying into route_label, or better, never persist raw PII in label column. canonicalizer should hash->id mapping.
ravi: agree. canonicalizer will return a stable opaque id and we store hashed label for debugging only, with access limited.
taylor: next steps: draft PR for ingest changes (dual-write + header), design doc for backfill options with perf estimates, and a console feature flag PR. I'll open the PRs by EOD.
deploy-bot: PR #4521 merged into `main` by taylor — CI checks passed :white_check_mark:
monica: thanks. can someone own the export+bulk-load feasibility investigation?
sam: i'll take that. will ping infra for network egress limits.
jen: propose we schedule a short canary: run dual-write for 1% of traffic and monitor route mismatch rate and dashboard errors.
ravi: +1, also add a cheap metric: `route_mismatch_rate` (label->id failures) and `canonicalizer_latency`.
taylor: ok capturing: canary 1% -> 10% -> 100% with backfill running in parallel. hold on full switch until canonicalizer mismatch < 0.1% for 24h and backfill progress > 90%.
monica: sounds good. I'll add the rollout playbook to the doc and tag product for console feature flag UX.
jen: where do we list migration IDs? prefer central table `schema_migrations.telemetry_route_split`.
taylor: agreed.
sam: anything else? rollback plan?
monica: rollback: disable dual-write and point queries back to legacy view, ensure catalog mapping not used for quota. this should be low-risk.
taylor: cool. I'll post the design doc link and schedule a follow-up meeting tomorrow 11am.
monica: thanks all :rocket:
